sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-04 against the files, the Figshare record and the paper's Methods (Gardner et al. 2022, PMC8810387). Files: the zip's MD5 and size are those Figshare publishes (379bfdca..., 319,902,753 bytes); its SHA-256 was computed from one full download, and each member read is pinned by its own SHA-256. Pickles: the three spikes_mod arrays import only numpy.core.multiarray._reconstruct, numpy.ndarray and numpy.dtype, listed from their opcodes before any runs. Units: 483 (166, 168 and 149 in modules 1 to 3), within the paper's 'from 140 to 544 grid cells per session' and its 66 to 189 grid cells per module. Time: the sessions text gives open_field_1 from 7457 to 16045 s with valid_times 7457-14778 and 14890-16045 s; the 858,800 samples kept run from 7457.01 to 16045.00 s every 0.01 s (100 Hz); the spikes kept run from 7457.02 to 16045.00 s; the file's samples and spikes continue to 21640 s through the two wagon-wheel sessions, which are not loaded. Space: x from -73.0 to 74.8 cm and y from -73.5 to 74.0 cm (a 147.8 x 147.5 cm span) against the stated 1.5 x 1.5 m box, so the unit is metres; the fitted square is centred at (0.75, 0.16) cm and rotated 0.42 deg, and no tracked sample lies outside it. Heading: azimuth minus the direction of movement above 10 cm/s has a circular mean of -4.8 deg and a median spread of 20.6 deg. Looked at: the overview figure (the path fills the square; occupancy has a few unvisited bins at the walls; heading minus travel is concentrated near 0) and three animation frames, whose position and heading arrow agree with the overview's x and y traces at the same times.
